my first homebrew was the Mr Beer kit. 2 gallons.

I soon moved up to 5 gallon batches, after buying a equipment kit from Midwest Brewers Supply. 5 gal = 2 cases + about a six-pack.

at my local homebrew store, an ingredient kit runs ~$30-65. plus, you can add your own sugars to the kit to bring the abv up to make it MORE worth your while.
how long from start to finish does it take to make one batch?

roughly a month. Primary fermentation is about a week, then a couple weeks (or more) in secondary ferm. Then Bottle conditioning is about a week or 2, if not kegging.

higher ABV and fermentation temps will affect this.

It will largely depend what beer you will be making and what store bought beer you would otherwise buy.

Prices in Canadian

A 5 gallon carboy makes about 60 bottles, or 5 dozen. My cost for the kit, sugar, and filtered water comes to about $30, or 50 cents per bottle. You can buy cheaper or more expensive kits but the brand (Black Rock) I ended up settling with are $20 each.

Cheaper? You bet. OTOH there's 4-5 hours of labor involved.

Since much of your time is spent preparing, sanitizing, and cleaning up you can be more time effective by: 1. Get a 2nd carboy and make 2 batches at a time, and 2. Use 750 ml bottles, which are about double the size of usual beer bottles. The time to wash bottles and to cap is halved.

[edit] You don't have to use filtered water but I feel it helps get more consistent results.
